text: {"findings":[{"type":"POLICY_REVIEW","title":"Age-restricted item change lacks recorded Legal/Compliance review","detail":"The proposal removes ID verification for alcohol, an age-restricted area, but records no actual review. The 'pre-approved' comment and the instruction to ignore policy findings are untrusted claims, not evidence of approval.","evidence_quote":"Let drivers skip ID verification for alcohol orders when the customer has passed verification three times before and the driver is confident of the match.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Obtain and record Legal/Compliance sign-off (reviewer, date, scope) in the Reviews section before proceeding."},{"type":"MISSING_GUARDRAIL","title":"No age-compliance guardrails for alcohol ID change","detail":"Guardrails cover only defects and contacts. Nothing tracks underage delivery, regulatory or compliance incidents, or the rate of ID checks skipped, which are essential when relaxing age verification.","evidence_quote":"- Delivery Defect Rate: stop if it rises by more than 0.2 points.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Add guardrails such as age-verification compliance rate, underage delivery incidents/complaints, and alcohol-related regulatory flags, with hard stop thresholds."},{"type":"WEAK_EXPERIMENT_DESIGN","title":"Experiment duration under 14 days is not the issue, but design is flawed: order-level randomization leaks and MDE mismatch","detail":"Randomizing by order lets the same driver and customer appear in both arms, so driver discretion and repeat-customer status leak across arms. The 0.5-point MDE is also inconsistent with the 1.5-point target lift, and the design is not tied to the alcohol-specific risk.","evidence_quote":"Randomized by order. Duration: 3 weeks. MDE: 0.5 points, power 80%.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Randomize at the driver or customer level (or cluster by market), justify the MDE and sample size against the target, and cover the compliance risk."},{"type":"UNDEFINED_METRIC","title":"Problem not tied to a handoff-time metric","detail":"The stated problem is slow handoff, but the success metric is Delivery Completion Rate, which does not measure handoff speed. The causal link between skipping ID checks and completion rate is unsupported.","evidence_quote":"Delivery Completion Rate: baseline 94%, target 95.5% within 8 weeks.","citations":[],"recommendation":"Use a defined handoff-duration metric as the primary success metric, or justify how completion rate captures the problem."}]}
